questions: Should the x-values for each line be sequential integers starting from 1, regardless of the length or content of the inner list?
Are the y-values to be shuffled the actual elements of the inner list, or should they be sequential integers (like indices) derived from the list's length?
If an inner list contains non-numeric elements (e.g., strings), how should they be handled when plotting as y-values?
Is the length of each line (number of points) determined by the length of the original inner list, or by the number of elements after some filtering (e.g., removing None)?
Should the function create a new figure and axes each time it's called, or reuse an existing one if provided?
Is the order of lines plotted correspond to the order of inner lists in `list_of_lists`, even if some are empty and skipped?
Should the function set any plot title, labels, or other formatting before returning?
If `list_of_lists` is empty or contains only empty lists, what should be returned? An empty figure/axes or handle gracefully?
